edges.effect_quant: A 2025 meta-analysis of 13 randomized trials (n=670) found that polyphenol-rich interventions increased acetate and butyrate, consistent with improved microbial function. Smaller randomized crossover trials in healthy or metabolic-risk adults also reported higher Bifidobacterium and other favorable taxa after red wine polyphenol exposure.
edges.population: adults consuming polyphenol-rich foods or beverages such as red wine, berries, cocoa, and other plant-derived interventions
edges.mechanism: Polyphenols can shift microbiome health by selectively favoring bacterial groups that metabolize complex plant compounds into short-chain fatty acids and other bioactive metabolites. The resulting pattern is less about one universal diversity boost and more about reproducible increases in beneficial taxa and microbial fermentation products in responsive hosts.
edges.summary: Dietary polyphenols generally look supportive of microbiome health, but the effect is food-specific and not perfectly uniform across studies. The strongest human evidence points to improved short-chain fatty acid production and selective increases in taxa like Bifidobacterium or butyrate producers, rather than a dramatic across-the-board diversity effect.
edges.caveats: This edge bundles several polyphenol sources together, so effect size and microbial signatures vary by matrix, dose, and host metabolic state. Some trials show only modest or selective changes, which is why the evidence is better described as promising and biologically coherent than definitive.

evidence.notes: Effect of Polyphenol-Rich Interventions on Gut Microbiota and Inflammatory or Oxidative Stress Markers in Adults Who Are Overweight or Obese: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

evidence.citation: Queipo-Ortuno et al 2012 Am J Clin Nutr
evidence.notes: Influence of red wine polyphenols and ethanol on the gut microbiota ecology and biochemical biomarkers.
Red wine polyphenols modulate fecal microbiota and reduce markers of the metabolic syndrome in obese patients.
